name: Covetousness and the Love of Money

counsel.text: Sin aims always at the utmost; every time it rises up to tempt or entice, might it have its own course, it would go out to the utmost sin in that kind. Every unclean thought or glance would be adultery if it could; every covetous desire would be oppression, every thought of unbelief would be atheism, might it grow to its head.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 2

counsel.text: Water is useful for the sailing of the ship: all the danger is when the water gets into the ship; so the fear is, when the world gets into the heart.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the tenth commandment

counsel.text: It is a sin that wears a cloak, it cloaks itself under the name of frugality and good husbandry. It has many pleas and excuses for itself; more than any other sin: as providing for one's family. The more subtle the sin is, the less discernible it is.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the tenth commandment

counsel.text: The root of covetousness is distrust of God's providence. Faith believes that God will provide; that he who feeds the birds will feed his children; that he who clothes the lilies will clothe his lambs; and thus faith overcomes the world. Faith is the cure of care. It not only purifies the heart, but satisfies it; it makes God our portion, and in him we have enough.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the tenth commandment

counsel.text: The fourth remedy is to pray for a heavenly mind. Lord, let the loadstone of thy Spirit draw my heart upward. Lord, dig the earth out of my heart; teach me how to possess the world, and not love it; how to hold it in my hand, and not let it get into my heart.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the tenth commandment

counsel.text: Set faith at work on Christ for the killing of thy sin. His blood is the great sovereign remedy for sin-sick souls. Live in this, and thou wilt die a conqueror; yea, thou wilt, through the good providence of God, live to see thy lust dead at thy feet.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Faithful Father, the earth is yours and everything in it, and you have promised never to leave or forsake your children. I come through Jesus Christ. I confess that I have coveted. I have wanted more than you have given, and I have set my heart on things that will perish. I have trusted money for a security that belongs to you alone, and I have measured my life by the abundance of my possessions. My covetousness is idolatry. I have tried to serve two masters, and I have been stingy toward you and toward my neighbor. Forgive me, Lord. Christ, though he was rich, became poor for my sake. He is my treasure, and in him I have an inheritance that can never perish, spoil, or fade. For his sake pardon me. Holy Spirit, put this greed to death, and make me content and generous. Teach me to lay up treasure in heaven. I thank you that you did not spare your own Son, and that with him you will graciously give me all things. In Jesus' name. Amen.

prayers.title: When I want more
prayers.text: Lord, I am wanting what I do not have, and my heart is pulled toward it. Stop me and turn me back to you. You are my portion, and you know what I need before I ask. Remind me that life does not consist in the abundance of possessions, and that I brought nothing into the world and can take nothing out. Help me give thanks for what you have already given, and give something away today. Lord Jesus, be my treasure. Amen.

prayers.title: For a generous heart
prayers.text: Father, you love a cheerful giver, for you are the most generous Giver of all. Make me like you. Loosen my grip on money and things. Teach me to hold them as a steward and not an owner, and to use them for your glory and my neighbor's good. Make me honest in my work, faithful in my giving, and free from the love of money. Let me be rich in good works and ready to share. Fix my hope not on uncertain riches but on you, who richly provide everything for me to enjoy. Through Jesus Christ. Amen.

examinationQuestions: What did you want today that you did not have, and what did you think having it would give you that God has not already given you in Christ?
Where have you looked to money or possessions for the safety, comfort, or worth that only God can give?
Where has covetousness dressed itself up as wisdom, thrift, or providing for those you love?
Have work, buying, or planning how to get more crowded out prayer, the Word, or the Lord's Day this week?
When did you last give freely to your church or to someone in need, and did you give gladly?
If God took away what you own tomorrow, would Christ still be enough for you? Ask God to make it so.
fleeActions: Close the shopping page or app and put your phone down. Do not buy anything today that you had not planned to buy this morning.
Write down three things God has given you this week, and thank him for each one out loud.
Give something away today, quietly: money to your church's deacons, or help to someone in need.
Open your Bible to Matthew 6:19-34 and read it slowly. Then pray it back to God in your own words.
Message a brother or sister in your church and tell them honestly that you are fighting greed. Ask them to pray for you today.
Go and do the next task of your calling with your whole heart, as work for the Lord and not for gain.

afterFallReadings.text: God can bestow a jewel upon us, but we fall so in love with it, that we forget Him that gave it.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 10

afterFallReadings.text: Yea, let me add, that never any soul did or shall perish by the power of any lust, sin, or corruption, who could raise his soul by faith to an expectation of relief from Jesus Christ.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14
